webtoon-shot-v1, one finished original vertical-scroll webtoon art shot, 1280x3840 tall composite canvas, exactly 3 equal-height full-width mini-panels stacked vertically with clean white gutters, preserve 1:3 proportion, 5% safe margin. Read top-to-bottom as one continuous transition. Purpose: sensory deepening transition from present table crumbs to ashes and ledger of Arken’s fall. Top-down insert shot, portrait lens feel, very close camera tracking the tiny material under a child’s fingertip, subtle pull-out movement across panels. 

Panel 1: full-width. Warm dim indoor light over a dark wooden fortress dining table. At left side only, the small fingertip and blue-gray sleeve of a seven-year-old boy Theo Waldhart, no face visible, no adult hand, tiny child hand only. One small bread crumb remains stuck at the fingertip. Focus on texture of crumb and wood grain. 

Panel 2: full-width. Same crumb in the exact corresponding position, now suspended in windless dark neutral space, transforming into pale gray ash fragments and dust, drifting downward. Background nearly colorless, soft emptiness. Linework loosens into ash. Lighting warmth disappears. 

Panel 3: full-width. The falling ash lands on an old worn ledger with a black-brown cover and on cracked stone floor beside it, becoming the entrance into a ruined past. Ledger edges regain sharpness, but no readable text anywhere. Muddy brown-gray atmosphere, heavy memory mood. The ash aligns with the same central trajectory from prior panels. 

Visual continuity: material in same vertical position across all three panels, seamless time/location transition. Color progression from beige bread crumb to gray ash to dark brown-black ledger. Soft 2D webtoon rendering, painterly anime-inspired linework, no duplicate character, no speech bubbles, no captions, no watermark, no signature, no readable writing.
